judge.verdict: Mostly adequate; garbled proper nouns and a broken final clause
judge.rationale: MT conveys the core facts (Catalan and Spanish official, ~half prefer Catalan, most understand it, nearly all know Spanish) but garbles names (Barcelona->Balelona, Catalan->katlan/katalan), uses singular 'is' for two languages, and the final clause 'understand it almost all Spanish' drops the verb 'knows', losing/garbling the distinct 'everyone knows Spanish' fact — hence reduced adequacy and low fluency. The back-transcribed audio actually normalizes 'katlan'->'Catalan' and loses no meaning versus MT (only the proper noun 'Ballalona' stays garbled, and the same truncated final clause remains), so e2e adequacy is on par with, and slightly above, MT adequacy since no meaning was dropped in TTS.

mt_text: The high tower or burial ground in the burial valley of the Egyptian tomb has many pyramids in which the Great Pyramid is the largest pyramid many small monuments and alma mater statues.
back_transcript: the high tower or burial ground in the burial valley of the egyptian tomb has many pyramids in which the great pyramid is the largest perum it many small monuments and alma-mata statues

judge.verdict: Core pyramid facts intact; key landmarks mistranslated
judge.rationale: MT correctly conveys the central claim (an Egyptian burial valley with many pyramids of which the Great Pyramid is the largest), but loses or corrupts most named entities: 'Giza' is dropped, 'cao nguyên/plateau' becomes 'high tower', 'small tombs' becomes 'small monuments', and critically 'đại nhân sư/Great Sphinx' becomes 'alma mater statues'. About half the referential content is wrong, so adequacy is moderate. Fluency is only fair: readable and mostly grammatical, but the trailing list ('...largest pyramid many small monuments and alma mater statues') is a run-on with no verb or conjunction binding it to the main clause. For e2e, the audio transcript matches the MT almost exactly; the only genuine loss is 'pyramid'->'perum it' in 'largest pyramid' (a redundant instance, since pyramids are already established), while 'alma-mata' vs 'alma mater' is mere back-transcription spelling and not penalized, so e2e tracks MT adequacy with a slight deduction.
